excerpt_i18n.en: The AI short drama industry has moved beyond "wild growth" and officially entered a new phase focused on quality and scale. However, while most creators still rely on an "AI blind box" approach, three harsh realities have already emerged: Uncontrollable creative process—relying on AI "card-drawing" random generation easily leads to character facial changes, position drifting, and lack of narrative logic between shots. Difficulty balancing quality and output—fully automatic generation often feels mechanical, while manual refinement struggles to support mass delivery. Difficulty coordinating team management—multi-creator projects lack standardized tools, making it hard to uniformly manage project progress, computing costs, and review data. The barrier to creating high-quality AI short dramas lies not in generating one or two good shots, but in stably maintaining character positions and performances throughout the entire work. To address this, the Tiangong Short Drama Workbench has launched a new dual-track creation model—"Agent Intelligent Storyboarding + Infinite Canvas"—redefining the high-quality AI short drama production pipeline.

excerpt_i18n.en: On July 16, international authoritative consulting firm IDC released its 2025 China AI programming market share report, which shows that Alibaba leads with a 47.6% market share, surpassing the combined total of second to fifth place, continuing to dominate China's AI programming market. AI programming is one of the fastest areas for global large model application deployment and a key competitive battleground for top model startups and tech companies. The IDC report indicates that the 2025 China AI programming market size is 399 million RMB, expected to grow rapidly to 1.173 billion RMB by the end of 2026. Alibaba's core AI programming product Qoder holds a 47.6% market share, far ahead of domestic peers. Zhipu CodeGeeX, SenseTime Raccoon, Tencent CodeBuddy, and Baidu Comate rank second to fifth with shares of 11.5%, 10.5%, 6.9%, and 6.0%, respectively. IDC analysts note that AI coding is evolving from a "code generation tool" to a "software productivity platform." With continuous enhancements in large model reasoning capabilities, autonomous execution by agents, and enterprise code asset management, AI coding is no longer limited to code completion but gradually covers the full software lifecycle, including requirements analysis, coding development, testing and verification, and operations delivery. As one of the earliest domestic programming tools, Qoder now possesses intelligent agent capabilities.

excerpt_i18n.en: Yunbao Intelligent, a domestic DPU maker, submitted its IPO application to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange's ChiNext board on June 30, becoming the first DPU chip company to file under the fourth set of listing criteria. It is regarded by the market as "the first domestic DPU stock." However, as the prospectus disclosed operating data, two types of controversy emerged: three consecutive years of net losses attributable to the parent company and heavy revenue reliance on a single major customer. The implementation of ChiNext's fourth set of listing standards has completely broken the requirement that a listing must be profitable, precisely accommodating hard-tech firms like high-end chips that require heavy upfront investment and are not yet profitable. Resolving chip bottlenecks is a core national strategic task. Currently, among the three core computing chips in data centers, domestic substitution in the CPU and GPU tracks has achieved phased results, with local firms such as Haiguang, Huawei Kunpeng, Cambricon, and Huawei Ascend making continuous breakthroughs, gradually alleviating supply shortages. As the third key track in the computing power base, DPU has long been monopolized by overseas manufacturers and is a critical link in the AI industry chain that domestic substitution urgently needs to conquer. This is also a key policy consideration for the capital market in launching ChiNext's fourth set of listing standards, with a focus on supporting hard-tech DPU companies like Yunbao Intelligent. While the market has high expectations for Yunbao Intelligent as the "first DPU stock" to go public, there are also some doubts about it. These doubts essentially apply the profitability and customer evaluation standards of mature consumer enterprises and traditional manufacturing to evaluate high-end computing chip companies still in the early stages of commercialization.
